resources.title: CME Passport
resources.summary: Search activities by accredited providers. Check credit type, registration eligibility and the provider’s current activity page.

resources.title: CDC TRAIN
resources.summary: Find public-health learning with physician CME available on selected courses. TCEO retired at the end of 2025; start with CDC TRAIN.
resources.cost: Free CE on many courses; check each listing.

resources.title: PCSS-MOUD
resources.summary: Explore SAMHSA-supported substance-use training. For MATE, check the specific course’s eligibility, hours and completion evidence.

resources.title: AMA Ed Hub
resources.summary: Browse physician education and inspect the CME label. Free reading does not always include the quiz or credit claim.
resources.cost: Free account; some credit requires membership, subscription or a fee.

resources.title: AOA CME resources
resources.summary: Find live and on-demand osteopathic education. Verify the listed AOA category and your board’s acceptance.
resources.cost: Check activity pricing and membership access.

topics.title: Start with the requirement
topics.summary: Choose learning that fits the obligation you need to meet.
paragraphs: CME supports continued professional learning. License renewal, specialty certification and employer credentialing can ask for different evidence.
steps: Identify the organization receiving your credit.
Check its cycle, accepted categories and required topics.
Check the activity’s credit statement before enrolling.

topics.title: Check the credit type
paragraphs: AMA PRA Category 1 Credit and AOA categories use different systems. An accredited provider can also publish material that does not award CME.
AOA categories include 1-A, 1-B, 2-A and 2-B. Keep the category actually awarded; confirm the category mix your receiving board requires.
steps: Check the provider in the ACCME directory when applicable.
Read the activity’s designation and maximum credit.
Keep AMA, AOA, MOC and participation labels distinct.

topics.title: Plan for each license
paragraphs: Use the correct medical or osteopathic board.
steps: Record each license’s cycle.
Confirm accepted categories, topics and exceptions.
Review each activity against each intended use.

topics.title: Understand DEA MATE
topics.summary: Keep the one-time federal training requirement separate from recurring CME.
paragraphs: At the first applicable DEA registration or renewal on or after June 27, 2023, covered practitioners attest to meeting an accepted training standard. Solely veterinary practitioners are excluded.
Routes include specified addiction certification, qualifying recent education, or at least eight hours of eligible training. Earlier eligible training and cumulative sessions may count.
Eligible DEA training may also count toward state requirements when the state accepts it. Check each requirement before taking duplicate training.
steps: Read the DEA eligibility guidance for your situation.
Check the training source and keep completion evidence.
Do not automatically repeat eight hours at every renewal.

topics.title: Separate CME from board certification
topics.summary: Credit hours alone do not describe an entire certification program.
paragraphs: ABMS member boards set specialty-specific continuing-certification programs. Some CME activities also offer designated MOC credit. AOA certification uses its own OCC requirements.
steps: Check your certifying board’s current program and whether your licensing board recognizes certification activities toward CME.
Confirm the activity’s board-specific recognition and reporting requirements.
Keep board points separate from CME hours unless the activity explicitly awards both.

topics.title: Use CME Passport
topics.summary: Understand what appears in your record and how to bring it here.
paragraphs: Providers report completion to ACCME with your permission and matching information. Physicians cannot self-report completion into CME Passport.
steps: Ask the provider whether it reports your credit.
Check your Passport record after reporting.
Download your transcript and use Import transcript in CredentialDOMD. Review every row before saving.

topics.title: Keep usable evidence
paragraphs: Keep the original certificate or transcript. A saved file or progress bar is not a board decision.
steps: Review the provider, completion date, credit and category.
Check imported fields and duplicates.
Keep readable backups.

topics.title: Build a renewal plan
paragraphs: Leave time to claim credit and resolve missing evidence.
steps: Confirm your board’s cycle and deadline.
Review your evidence and remaining activities.
Check claim deadlines.
Complete the renewal application.

faqs.question: How many CME hours do I need?
faqs.answer: Check your licensing and certifying boards. This center does not assign a universal hour total or determine individual compliance.

faqs.question: Can I find CME without paying?
faqs.answer: Start with CDC TRAIN and PCSS-MOUD. Check that the specific activity awards physician CME and includes the certificate or credit claim at no charge.

faqs.question: How do I know an activity awards physician CME?
faqs.answer: Look for its credit designation, maximum available credit and completion requirements. Provider accreditation alone does not make every resource a CME activity.

faqs.question: Are AMA and AOA categories interchangeable?
faqs.answer: Do not automatically convert AMA Category 1 into AOA Category 1-A. Preserve the original credit type and confirm acceptance with the receiving organization.

faqs.question: What is AMA PRA Category 2 Credit?
faqs.answer: Physicians may self-document qualifying learning that is not certified for Category 1 under AMA criteria. It must be relevant to practice, non-promotional and meet the AMA’s educational and ethical standards. Check whether the receiving board accepts it; reading alone does not create Category 1 credit.

faqs.question: Are MOC points the same as CME hours?
faqs.answer: They are distinct credit designations. An activity may award both; verify each amount and board recognition rather than converting points into CME hours.

faqs.question: Can one activity help with more than one license?
faqs.answer: Confirm dates, topics and acceptance for each license. Do not assume reciprocity.

faqs.question: Can extra credits roll into my next cycle?
faqs.answer: Check the receiving board’s carryover rule before relying on surplus credit. Do not assume rollover.

faqs.question: Can I claim an exemption or waiver?
faqs.answer: Ask the relevant board about eligibility, evidence and approval. An AOA certification waiver does not change state-license requirements.

faqs.question: What if my certificate is missing?
faqs.answer: Check your provider account or request a replacement from the activity organizer. Keep the completion details while you resolve it. Do not invent a certificate.

faqs.question: Can I claim credit after a course expires?
faqs.answer: Check the activity’s credit-claim deadline and contact its provider. Reading material while it was available does not establish that a later claim is accepted.

faqs.question: How long should I keep CME records?
faqs.answer: Use your board’s retention and audit instructions. This center does not prescribe a universal retention period. Keep readable backups.

faqs.question: Why is an activity missing from CME Passport?
faqs.answer: Its provider may not have reported it, or matching details may need correction. Contact the provider; you cannot add completion credit yourself in Passport.

faqs.question: Does CredentialDOMD automatically sync with Passport?
faqs.answer: The available workflow is to download your Passport transcript and import it. Review the proposed entries before saving; this is not automatic account synchronization.

faqs.question: Do I repeat MATE training every DEA renewal?
faqs.answer: MATE is a one-time attestation requirement. Check the DEA guidance if your training history or eligibility is uncertain. State requirements remain separate.

faqs.question: Can earlier training satisfy MATE?
faqs.answer: Earlier eligible training, including qualifying DATA-waiver training, may count. Confirm the content and training source under DEA guidance and keep the evidence.

faqs.question: Do CredentialDOMD tutorials award CME?
faqs.answer: No. Our walkthroughs teach app tasks and use demo data. They do not award CME, MOC points or DEA training credit.

faqs.question: Does the app confirm that I am compliant?
faqs.answer: Its calculation depends on your saved records and rules on file. Review dates, categories and applicability, and confirm unresolved questions with the receiving board.

faqs.question: Does reported CME renew my license automatically?
faqs.answer: Reported credit is not proof that renewal is complete. Check your board’s application and confirmation requirements.
